title: The Workshop's fruit: John Vodakovich on drums and the group Trinity
summary: Without David Lee he struggled to find a drummer and used John Vodakovich, despite criticism, later playing with David Lee and James Singleton in Trinity.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: And the workshop did bear fruit. The workshop did bear fruit.

It bore many, many beautiful fruit. One of the things that I remember with the absence of David Lee, one of the things I remember with the absence of David Lee, it was very, very frustrating to try to find a drummer that could even play the concept. And when I began to form jazz groups later, one of the first groups that I, when I came back from New York and my travels, one of the first groups I formed had John Vodakovich on drums. And guys would come from the racial aspect. What are you doing with that white boy on drums? Why are you using him when there's so-and-so, there's James Black, there's Smokey Johnson, there's so-and-so. But because John was at the workshop every night for a long period of time, and one of his, besides his special sensitivity and his uniqueness in playing, he more than anybody else understood the concept of what I was looking for. And David had been a major influence in his playing. And nobody else that I played with gave me, even came close to what I had been getting from David, except that John knew and colored and played the melodic kind of drums, as well as bringing to it what he had learned from the experience. And, uh, pretty much, that was my favorite and main drummer, uh, for a number of years. And then gradually it rolled around, and then, uh, when David finally came back to New Orleans, there was a period of difficulty where we were not yet together. But since that whole thing has transpired, it's been a unity and a healing where we're now playing some music that's magical, and we've had, like, one of the best musical experiences that I've been, uh, that I've had with, uh, David Lee and James Singleton and I with a group that we call Trinity. Uh, when we put that particular force together, that's sometimes the closest to the magic of the experience that I had at the workshop. And it has, I mean, I'm sure new music is coming from that, and there are things that we're putting together and forces that bring about new music that, uh, fortunately, from that, we get a foundation that will be the, uh, the seed to the kind of fruit that you'll hear in the future.
